title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search
supports: AI features use core ranking and the Search index with query fan-out; AEO and GEO are SEO to Google; myths (no llms.txt, special markup, chunking, AI rewriting, inauthentic mentions or special schema needed); page-per-fan-out-query is scaled content abuse; eligibility needs the Search Console inclusion setting; caution about third-party tools

title: A new resource for optimizing for generative AI in Google Search (15 May 2026)
publisher: Google Search Central blog, John Mueller
supports: Publication date and scope of Google's generative AI optimisation guide

title: AI features and your website
supports: How AI Overviews and AI Mode pick links (query fan-out, different models), eligibility, no extra requirements, preview controls (nosnippet, data-nosnippet, max-snippet, noindex), traffic counted in the Web search type

title: Search generative AI control in Search Console
supports: Include or Exclude setting for AI Overviews, AI Mode and Discover AI features; Include is the default; exclusion in 1 to 2 days; no effect on other ranking or on training; live for all sites by 31 August 2026

title: Generative AI performance report (Search)
supports: Impressions-only report for AI Overviews and AI Mode with pages, countries, devices and dates; 1,000-row limit; Labs excluded; rolled out to all sites by 31 August 2026

title: Google's common crawlers (Google-Extended)
supports: Google-Extended controls Gemini training and grounding in Gemini Apps and Vertex AI; no effect on Search inclusion or ranking; robots.txt token only

title: Supporting a shared AI training control for websites (30 October 2026)
publisher: Google Search Central blog, John Mueller
supports: Google plans to honour the IETF AIPREF training-preference token in robots.txt in 2027; treated as a Google-Extended disallow when Google-Extended is not named; allowing Google-Extended keeps Gemini Apps grounding eligibility

title: Google Search's guidance on using third-party SEO tools, services, and advice
supports: No tool has access to Google's internal ranking data; be wary of tools promising AI search results; Search Console is the first-party source

title: Organization structured data
supports: Organization markup helps Google tell an organisation apart; recommended properties (name, url, logo, sameAs, address, identifiers); no required properties; place on home or About page

title: [GA4] Default channel group
supports: AI Assistant default channel (medium ai-assistant) listing ChatGPT, Gemini, Deepseek, Copilot and Grok; AI Overviews and AI Mode stay in Organic Search

title: Overview of OpenAI crawlers
supports: OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User and OAI-AdsBot: what each does, robots.txt effects, about 24 hours to take effect, published IP lists

title: Publishers and developers FAQ
publisher: OpenAI Help Center (confirmed by search result; the page blocks automated fetches)
supports: Any public site can appear in ChatGPT search; do not block OAI-SearchBot; ChatGPT adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to referral links

title: Where ChatGPT search results come from: Google, Bing, Web IQ and 8+ providers (September 2026)
supports: Vendor analysis inferring that ChatGPT uses its own index plus at least eight outside providers (including Microsoft Web IQ, Google results via scrapers, Yelp and Tripadvisor); Bing mainly in Deep Research; stated confidence levels and conflict of interest

title: Perplexity crawlers
supports: PerplexityBot for search results, not training; Perplexity-User for user requests, generally ignores robots.txt; up to 24 hours to take effect; IP lists

title: How does Perplexity work?
supports: Real-time web search with numbered citations; no published ranking criteria for sources

title: Perplexity is using stealth, undeclared crawlers to evade website no-crawl directives (4 August 2025)
supports: Test showing undeclared crawling after blocks; request volumes; Cloudflare de-listed Perplexity as a verified bot; ChatGPT-User respected the block in the same test

title: Does Anthropic crawl data from the web, and how can site owners block the crawler?
supports: ClaudeBot, Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot and the effect of blocking each; robots.txt and Crawl-delay honoured; IP blocking not advised; general no-AI-training signal honoured

title: Introducing AI Performance in Bing Webmaster Tools Public Preview (10 February 2026)
supports: Citation reporting for Copilot, Bing AI summaries and partners (total citations, cited pages, grounding queries, page-level counts) and Microsoft's advice for earning citations, including IndexNow and Bing Places

title: Optimizing your content for inclusion in AI search answers (8 October 2025)
publisher: Microsoft Advertising blog, Krishna Madhavan (Microsoft Bing)
supports: How Microsoft's AI systems break pages into pieces and choose them; structure advice; mistakes such as answers hidden in tabs, PDFs or images; no guarantee of selection

title: Announcing new options for webmasters to control usage of their content in Bing Chat (22 September 2023)
supports: NOCACHE and NOARCHIVE meta tags and their effect on Bing chat answers and AI training; pages stay in Bing search results

title: The /llms.txt file
supports: llms.txt proposed on 3 September 2024; format; aimed at inference-time use; described as a proposal open to input, not a formal standard

title: We Analyzed 137K Sites: 97% of llms.txt Files Never Get Read (15 June 2026)
supports: 28% of 137,210 sites had a valid llms.txt (upper bound); 97% of those got no requests in May 2026; bot shares and caveats

title: llms.txt shows no clear effect on AI citations, based on 300k domains (20 November 2025)
publisher: Search Engine Journal, Matt G. Southern (reporting SE Ranking's study)
supports: About 10% adoption across roughly 300,000 domains and no measurable link between llms.txt and AI citation frequency

title: GEO: Generative Engine Optimization (Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024)
supports: The GEO framework and GEO-bench; adding quotations, statistics and citations raised source visibility by up to about 40% in tests; keyword stuffing did not help; results vary by domain

title: Generative Engine Optimization: How to Dominate AI Search (Chen, Wang, Chen and Koudas, September 2025)
supports: AI search engines favour earned (third-party) media over brand-owned and social content more than Google does; engines differ in diversity, freshness and phrasing sensitivity

title: Google users are less likely to click on links when an AI summary appears in the results (22 July 2025)
supports: March 2025 browsing data from 900 US adults: share of searches with AI summaries, click rates with and without summaries, query length effect, most-cited sources

title: Update: 38% of AI Overview Citations Pull From The Top 10 (2 March 2026)
supports: 37.9% of AI Overview cited URLs also ranked in the top 10 for the query (863,000 SERPs), down from about 76% in July 2025, with method caveats

title: An Analysis of AI Overview Brand Visibility Factors (75K Brands Studied) (26 May 2025)
supports: Branded web mentions correlated most with AI Overview brand visibility (0.664), well above backlinks (0.218); correlation only

title: AIO Impact on Google CTR: September 2025 Update (4 November 2025)
supports: Organic CTR on AI Overview queries fell 61% from June 2024 to September 2025; brands cited in the AI Overview had higher organic and paid CTR than uncited ones; no proof of cause

title: AI recommendations change with nearly every query: SparkToro (30 January 2026)
publisher: Search Engine Journal, Matt G. Southern (reporting SparkToro and Gumshoe research)
supports: 2,961 runs of 12 prompts on ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI returned the same brand list less than 1 in 100 times; appearance rate across runs steadier than order; conflict-of-interest note
